newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Indians blockade Paranapanema tin mine.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Indians blockade Paranapanema tin mine.

text.p: Indians demanding increased compensation are blockading the Pitinga tin mine of Brazil's mining concern Grupo Paranapanema but neither production nor sales are being affected, a company director said.

Helio Blak, Director of Finance and Market Relations, told Reuters the Indians of the Waimiri-Atroari tribe had been stopping trucks for three days from leaving or entering the mine in Amazonas state.
"This is not stopping production nor sales. We have stocks outside the area of both mineral and metal for four months," Blak said.

The Indians were demanding an increase to 80,000 reais a month from 16,000 reais per month currently in the compensation Paranapanema pays to the local Waimiri-Atroari community in exchange for using roads through its reserve.
Paranapanema has offered 24,000 reais per month, Blak said.
"We are all interested in resolving this problem. We don't want any difficulties," he added.
Blak said Pitinga was currently producing 2,000 tonnes a month of tin concentrate and had reserves to maintain production at that level for another seven years.
Together with its Bom Futuro tin mine, Paranapanema produces between 1,100-1,200 tonnes of metal a month, exporting 80 percent of its production.

Blak said the Pitinga mine had an airfield. Staff and, as a last resort, minerals, could be flown in and out. The government's National Indian Foundation (Funai) was acting as intermediary between the company and the 700-strong local Indian community.
